label: Bible Study
prompt: The voice of him that crieth in the _____, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
verse: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
note: All four Gospels apply this voice to John the Baptist, preparing the way.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Thy shoes shall be iron and brass; and as thy days, so shall thy _____ be.
verse: Thy shoes shall be iron and brass; and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.
note: Moses's blessing on Asher: as thy days, so shall thy strength be — strength measured out to match each day.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great _____ knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
verse: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
note: Peter's rooftop vision: a great sheet let down by its four corners, full of creatures he'd never eat.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his _____ turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
verse: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
note: Solomon's foreign wives slowly turned the wisest king's heart to their gods.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: How shall we escape, if we _____ so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
verse: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
note: Hebrews' first warning: the danger isn't rejecting so great salvation outright — it's simply to 'neglect' it.
